digest.top_line: HyTEC prostate SBRT TCP: EQD2 90 Gy (36.1 Gy/5fx) → 95% 5-yr TCP in low-intermediate risk; high risk needs EQD2 102 Gy (38.7 Gy/5fx).
digest.tldr: HyTEC/AAPM SBRT dose-response day across prostate, thoracic, liver and H&N, all pooled modeling of published series, no randomised data. Prostate led: 36.1 Gy/5fx → 95% 5-yr TCP in low-intermediate risk; urethra Dmax ≥47 Gy and rectal C39Gy ≥40% flag late toxicity. Stage I NSCLC LC plateaus at 50±1 Gy/5fx PTV periphery.

sites.intro: Two HyTEC prostate SBRT reviews: modeled TCP dose thresholds by risk group plus dose-volume toxicity constraints, neither from randomised data.

studies.name: Heterogeneous-dosing Prostate SBRT, 5-year Outcomes
studies.tldr: Urethra Dmax ≥47 Gy → late ≥G2 GU OR 4.2; rectal C39Gy ≥40% → ≥G3 GI OR 8.7 (HyTEC review; Fuller 5-yr data absent).
details: ⚠️ Source mismatch: title/DOI cite Fuller et al (Eur Urol Oncol 2018); full text is Wang et al HyTEC prostate SBRT toxicity review (IJROBP)
⚠️ No heterogeneous-dosing trial efficacy or 5-yr outcomes in source text; no effect size reported for that trial
🔍 AAPM working group review of prostate SBRT reports 2001-2018; SBRT defined as ≤5 fx
🔍 Excluded series <40 pts (except sexual outcomes), SBRT boost, proton, non-English, acute-only

details.text: 📐 NTCP-derived dose thresholds (authors' refits of published patient data)
📊 Prescription dose vs late toxicity (Sunnybrook series)

details: 📊 Heterogeneity: UCSF hotspot-heavy plans had more CTCAE G2-3 urinary toxicity; no effect size reported in source
📊 At 50 Gy/5 fx: 6 of 61 pts (10%) CTCAE G3-4 rectal toxicity, 5 needing colostomy

subdetails: Prostate >60 cc: late G2-3 urinary 15% vs 8%
Prior TURP: late G2-3 hematuria 21% vs 2%
QD vs QOD (Stanford): late G1-2 urinary 56% vs 17%, bowel 44% vs 5%

details: 🔗 2018 ASTRO/ASCO/AUA guideline advised Rx ≤36.25 Gy; authors read ≥G3 risk as low up to 40 Gy
⚠️ QD vs QOD gap may reflect early-era learning curve, per authors
⚠️ Thin events (Kim: 6 events) give wide ORs; authors state firm constraints cannot be made

verdict.rationale: Full text is the HyTEC prostate SBRT toxicity review (Wang et al), not the Fuller heterogeneous-dosing trial; no trial outcomes to classify.

studies.significance: The heterogeneity signal transfers: UCSF plans with larger hotspots carried more G2-3 urinary toxicity, and urethra Dmax ≥47 Gy (5-fx equivalent) tracked late ≥G2 urinary toxicity (OR 4.2). For CyberKnife plans prescribed to low isodose lines, prescription isodose and OAR Dmax may matter as much as nominal Rx dose.
studies.monday_clinic: In low-intermediate risk prostate cancer considered for 4-5 fx SBRT, a prostate >60 cc, prior TURP, or anticoagulant use flags higher late urinary or bowel risk in this review; it says nothing about cancer control or the Fuller heterogeneous-dosing outcomes.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Systematic PubMed review of prostate SBRT reports from **2001-2018** by an AAPM working group (HyTEC series), with NTCP modeling on the **4 studies** that published dose/outcome data. **Not** the Fuller heterogeneous-dosing trial named in the metadata.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Mostly **low-intermediate risk** prostate cancer. Excluded series with **<40 pts** (except sexual outcomes), SBRT boost, proton series, non-English reports and acute-only toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: SBRT defined as **≤5 fractions**; reviewed regimens mostly **35-40 Gy in 4-5 fx**. All used daily image guidance (CyberKnife fiducial tracking, Calypso, pretreatment fiducial imaging).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: At the **50 Gy/5 fx** dose level, 6 of 61 pts (10%) had CTCAE G3-4 rectal toxicity, 5 needing temporary or permanent colostomy. Sexual outcomes tracked baseline patient factors, **not** penile bulb dose.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Sits beneath the **2018 ASTRO/ASCO/AUA** guideline, which advised against Rx above **36.25 Gy** and favored QOD delivery; the authors read ≥G3 risk as low up to **40 Gy**. Efficacy vs conventional fractionation is deferred to **PACE** and **NRG-GU005**, with HYPO-RT-PC cited for 7-fx parity.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents 4-5 fx photon SBRT in low-intermediate risk prostate cancer. Does not represent SBRT boost, salvage after prior RT, proton plans, or cancer-control outcomes.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Mixed scales (RTOG, CTCAE v3/v4, EPIC, IPSS) and late windows from 3 months to years block pooling. NTCP fits rest on few events (Kim: **6 events**, OR CI 1.3-59.4), and the authors state **firm constraints cannot be made**.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: High-dose OAR metrics recur across urinary and bowel domains, so the authors set a Dmax-type constraint plus a moderate-dose volume limit as the minimum. Prescription isodose line and plan heterogeneity may weigh as much as nominal Rx, which bears directly on heterogeneous-dosing SBRT.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Urethra Dmax ≥47 Gy (OR 4.2), rectal C39Gy ≥40% (OR 8.7) and bladder mean ≥17 Gy (OR 7.7) are the modeled high-risk thresholds. The authors' floor is a Dmax-type constraint plus a moderate-dose volume limit, with plan heterogeneity and prescription isodose weighed alongside Rx dose.

studies.name: Prostate SBRT TCP Modeling and Systematic Review
studies.tldr: Low-intermediate risk: EQD2 90 Gy (36.1 Gy/5fx) gives 95% 5-yr TCP; high risk needs EQD2 102 Gy (38.7 Gy/5fx) for 95%.
details: 🔍 AAPM HyTEC systematic review + Poisson TCP dose-response model; endpoint FFBR
🔍 25 cohorts, 4,821 pts; literature through March 2018

details.text: 📊 Modeled 5-yr TCP (FFBR) by risk group, α/β=1.5 Gy

details: 📊 Risk mix: 2,235 low, 1,894 intermediate, 446 high risk
💊 Regimens 32-50 Gy in 4-5 fx; most prescriptions 35-40 Gy
🔍 All fiducial-guided; 16 cohorts Cyberknife, 7 linac
⚠️ Model fit only to cohorts with ≥5y f/u: 9 studies (1069 pts) low-intermediate, 3 studies (85 pts) high risk
⚠️ No cohort treated below EQD2 approximately 80 Gy, so the 71 Gy → 90% TCP point is extrapolated
⚠️ Dose modeled from prescription only, no DVH; target, margin and SV coverage varied widely
⚠️ Phoenix nadir+2 used in all but 3 cohorts; 2 used PSA decline trends
🔗 HYPO-RT-PC: 7-fx SBRT-like regimen matched conventional fractionation on control and toxicity at 5 yrs

verdict.rationale: Pooled nonrandomized, mostly single-institution series; dose modeled from prescription only, high-risk curve from 85 pts, low-intermediate 90% point extrapolated below the data.
verdict.audience: Localized prostate cancer, low/intermediate risk, definitive SBRT ≤5 fx

studies.significance: The 90% TCP anchor for low-intermediate risk (EQD2 71 Gy) lies below approximately 80 Gy, a range no reviewed cohort treated, so it is extrapolation. The data-backed read is 36.1 Gy/5fx at 95% TCP, which supports staying in the 35-40 Gy range rather than de-escalating below it.
studies.monday_clinic: In low- and intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer, this supports current SBRT prescriptions as sitting near the top of the dose-response curve; it does not extend to high-risk disease, where the fitted curve rests on 85 pts from 3 studies.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: AAPM WGSBRT (HyTEC) **systematic review plus Poisson TCP dose-response model**, endpoint **FFBR** (Phoenix nadir+2 in all but 3 cohorts). PubMed through March 2018; excluded series <40 pts, protons, >5 fx, and <6 Gy/fx.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **25 cohorts, 4,821 pts**: 2,235 low, 1,894 intermediate, 446 high risk (NCCN or D'Amico). Two registries (RSSR 437, RPCR 1743), 3 multi-institutional cohorts, the rest single-institution.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Regimens 32-50 Gy in 4-5 fx, total BED (α/β=1.5 Gy) 183.1-383.3 Gy; **most prescriptions 35-40 Gy in 4-5 fx**. All image-guided on implanted fiducials; target definition, PTV margins and SV coverage varied across institutions.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Model fit only on cohorts with ≥5y follow-up: **9 studies, 1069 pts** low-intermediate vs **3 studies, 85 pts** high risk.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Sits beside the conventionally fractionated dose-escalation RCTs that set the **≥75.6 Gy** standard, and HYPO-RT-PC, whose 7-fraction SBRT-like arm matched conventional fractionation on control and toxicity at 5 years. The pooled series here are nonrandomized, so this models dose-response within SBRT rather than comparing SBRT to EBRT.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents fiducial-guided, ≤5-fx photon SBRT monotherapy for low- and intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer. Does not represent high-risk disease, protons, SBRT boost after IMRT, or EQD2 below approximately 80 Gy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Dose is **prescription dose only**, with no dose-volume data, so margin and SV-coverage differences are invisible to the model. The low-intermediate 90% TCP point (EQD2 71 Gy) falls in the **region below approximately 80 Gy with no underlying data**.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Current 35-40 Gy prescriptions sit near the plateau for low-intermediate risk, so **further escalation buys little FFBR** there. High risk demands higher EQD2 for the same TCP, but the curve rests on too few, likely highly selected pts to anchor a prescription.

studies.interpretation:
The clinically useful output of this model is narrower than its abstract suggests. For low-intermediate risk, the defensible statement is that prescriptions in the common SBRT window already sit high on the dose-response curve, with EQD2 90 Gy (36.1 Gy in 5 fractions) mapping to 95% TCP at 5 years. The companion statement that EQD2 71 Gy reaches 90% TCP is weaker than it looks, because the figure legend itself concedes that the reviewed cohorts did not treat below approximately 80 Gy EQD2. That lower portion of the curve is the model's shape continued past the data, not an observation, and it should not be read as license to de-escalate below current practice.

The high-risk curve deserves even more caution. It was fit on 3 studies and 85 pts with at least 5 years of follow-up, drawn from a literature in which high-risk disease made up 446 of 4,821 pts overall. The authors acknowledge these are likely highly selected individuals. A curve built on that base can say that high-risk disease appears to need more dose for the same FFBR, which is biologically plausible, but the specific EQD2 targets of 97 and 102 Gy carry far more uncertainty than their precision implies. Variable ADT use across cohorts compounds this: hormone therapy alongside SBRT will lift FFBR independently of dose, and a prescription-level model cannot separate the two.

Methodologically, the central constraint is that dose enters the model only as prescription dose. Prostate SBRT plans differ in PTV margin, seminal vesicle coverage, prescription isodose and heterogeneity, and the review documents wide institutional variation in all of these. Two plans with the same nominal prescription can deliver quite different doses to the periphery of the gland, where extracapsular disease lives. The α/β of 1.5 Gy assumed for every EQD2 conversion is a further lever: a different value would reshuffle where each regimen falls on the axis. Most cohorts also had short follow-up, and only 5 had a median beyond 5 years, so the late biochemical failures that matter in a slow-growing disease are underrepresented.

Against the randomized evidence, this work does a different job. The conventional dose-escalation trials established that more dose improves control, and HYPO-RT-PC showed a 7-fraction SBRT-like schedule matching conventional fractionation at 5 years. This review cannot add comparative evidence, since every input is a nonrandomized series, but it does show that the 5-fraction literature as a whole is consistent with dose-response behavior and that the field converged on prescriptions near the plateau for favorable disease. Randomized SBRT data such as PACE-B postdate the search window and are the right place to test whether those prescriptions hold against conventional or moderate hypofractionation.

For a radiation oncologist, the practical reading is reassurance about current low-intermediate-risk prescriptions and a warning against treating the high-risk targets or the sub-80 Gy portion of the curve as validated. The questions the authors leave open (durability past 5 years, SBRT as a boost after pelvic IMRT, and MRI-based delineation shrinking the target) are exactly where prescription-only modeling stops being informative.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The data-supported point is 36.1 Gy/5fx at 95% TCP for low-intermediate risk; the 90% point at EQD2 71 Gy sits below approximately 80 Gy, where no cohort was treated. High-risk targets (EQD2 97 and 102 Gy) come from 85 pts, too thin to set a prescription.

sites.intro: Reirradiation SBRT for locally recurrent previously irradiated H&N: dose-response supports 40-50 Gy/5fx, with carotid blowout up to 10% to 20%.

studies.name: HyTEC H&N SBRT Tumor Control (AAPM WG)
studies.tldr: 3y LC 40% at 44.4 vs 15% at 26.8 Gy 5-fx equivalent (P<.01); 40-50 Gy/5fx suggested for locally recurrent previously irradiated H&N SBRT.
details: 🔍 AAPM HyTEC working group systematic review with pooled logistic dose-response modeling
🔍 8 publications, >300 cases of locally recurrent previously irradiated H&N cancer
🔍 Doses converted to 5-fx equivalent via LQ (Withers), nominal α/β 10 Gy
🔍 Only SBRT >6 weeks after primary RT included; boosts and benign tumors excluded
📊 2y LC dose-response also reached P<.01 for model and median split
📊 2y OS at highest doses almost double the lowest; ns (model P=.060, median split P=.13)

details.text: 🔍 Volume-adapted dose suggestion (not modeled; expert read from Rwigema data)
subdetails: <25 cm3: maximum 45 Gy/5fx equivalent, flat dose-response above this
Larger tumors: 45-50 Gy/5fx equivalent, consider novel escalation strategies

details: ⚠️ Carotid blowout reported in up to 10% to 20% even at lower doses
⚠️ Rwigema 2011 contributes one-third of cases, heavily shaping 2y and 3y fits
⚠️ Better-prognosis pts may have received higher dose; association, not causation
⚠️ HPV status, histology, concurrent cetuximab, QD vs QoD and tumor volume not modeled
⚠️ LC definitions mixed local and locoregional failure across series

verdict.rationale: Pooled model of 8 retrospective series; one-third of cases from one institution, LQ-converted representative doses, and possible selection of fitter pts for higher dose confound the dose-response.
verdict.audience: Unresectable locally recurrent, previously irradiated H&N cancer, SBRT reRT

studies.significance: Durability, not early response, is where dose matters: the 1y fit was flat (P=.096), while 2y and 3y LC tracked dose (P<.01), with 45 Gy/5fx modeled at 41% 3y LC. The WG ties escalation to volume, with a 45 Gy/5fx ceiling for <25 cm3 and 45-50 Gy for larger targets, weighed against carotid blowout in up to 10% to 20% of pts.
studies.monday_clinic: In unresectable, previously irradiated locally recurrent H&N cancer being weighed for SBRT reRT, this supports dose escalation over low-dose regimens when durable control is the goal; it does not extend to planned boosts <6 weeks from primary RT, de novo SBRT, or benign tumors.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: AAPM HyTEC working group **systematic review** with pooled logistic dose-response modeling (maximum likelihood, bootstrap CIs with 2000 samples). PubMed search identified 293 articles; **8 publications** with usable per-study dose and outcome data were modeled.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Locally recurrent, previously irradiated malignant H&N cancer**, largely unresectable, treated with SBRT **>6 weeks** after primary RT. Planned boosts and benign tumors were excluded; HPV status was unavailable for most series.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Mostly CyberKnife with thermoplastic mask and 6D skull tracking; contemporary series used GTV-to-PTV expansions of 2 to 6 mm. Each series' weighted PTV marginal dose was converted to a **5-fraction equivalent** at α/β 10 Gy.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary endpoints:** local control (local or locoregional, per series) at 1, 2 and 3 years, and OS at 1 and 2 years. KM values were digitized when not stated.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Dose-response was **ns at 1y** but reached **P<.01 at 2y and 3y** for LC; the 2y OS trend did not reach significance (model P=.060).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Carotid blowout syndrome reported in **up to 10% to 20%** of pts even at lower doses. Carotid toxicity risk is lower with non-consecutive-day fractionation; NTCP modeling sits in the companion working group report.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Surgical salvage remains SOC for resectable recurrence; this addresses the unresectable remainder. The pooled curve is anchored by Rwigema 2011 (four dose groups, one-third of cases) and spans Chua's single-fraction series through Lartigau's 36 Gy in 6 fractions with cetuximab in all pts.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents unresectable locally recurrent, previously irradiated malignant H&N cancer treated with SBRT >6 weeks after primary RT. Does not represent planned SBRT boosts, de novo primary SBRT, or benign tumors.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Tumor volume, the variable most likely to drive dose need, was **not in the model**, so the volume-adapted dose split is expert judgment. Numbers at risk at 2 and 3 years were not available, so weighting used initial N, and the significant fits rest on the thinnest data.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The signal is that dose buys **durability** of control rather than early response. The upper end of the suggested range for larger tumors sits at or beyond the highest pooled dose group median (44.4 Gy), so it is extrapolation that needs prospective testing against carotid risk.

studies.interpretation:
The working group's central claim is narrower than the headline dose range suggests. At 1 year the pooled curve does not separate dose levels with confidence (model P=.096), and only at 2 and 3 years does local control track dose (P<.01). Biologically that pattern is plausible: most recurrences may respond early regardless of dose, with the difference between regimens showing up as durability, which is the endpoint that matters for a patient who survives long enough to fail locally. Statistically it means the significant fits rest on the thinnest part of the data. Numbers at risk at 2 and 3 years are far smaller than at baseline and were not reported by most series, so the authors weighted by initial analyzable N, which overstates the information carried by the later timepoints.

The dose axis is itself a construction. Each series contributes one representative dose, converted to a 5-fraction equivalent with the linear-quadratic model at a nominal α/β of 10 Gy. At SBRT dose per fraction that conversion is the weakest link, and the authors concede it is likely a gross oversimplification. A single-fraction series and a six-fraction cetuximab series sit on the same axis only through that assumption. Rwigema 2011 contributes about one-third of the cases and four of the dose points, so the shape of the later curves is in large part one institution's experience, with its own selection, imaging and response criteria.

Confounding by indication is the larger threat. The authors flag that better-prognosis patients may have been treated more aggressively, so the OS trend (almost double at the highest doses, but not reaching significance) cannot be read as dose causing survival, and the same caution applies with less force to local control. HPV status, histology, concurrent cetuximab, every-other-day versus daily fractionation and tumor volume were all unmodeled. Volume matters most: the underlying Rwigema data indicate larger tumors need more dose for equivalent control, and a pooled curve that ignores volume could partly be a volume curve if smaller targets clustered in the higher-dose series.

What the analysis does move is the choice between low-dose SBRT and the 40 to 50 Gy 5-fraction equivalent range. For a patient with an unresectable in-field recurrence and a life expectancy long enough for durable control to matter, it is the best pooled argument against staying under 30 Gy. The volume-adapted split (a 45 Gy ceiling for small targets, 45 to 50 Gy for larger ones) is an expert reading rather than a model output, and the upper end sits at or beyond the highest dose group median in the pooled series (44.4 Gy), so it extrapolates past most of the evidence.

Toxicity is the counterweight the model leaves out. Carotid blowout has been reported in up to 10% to 20% of patients even at lower doses, so the escalation argument holds only with careful carotid-aware planning, and the cited data favouring non-consecutive-day delivery for carotid risk have not been tested for their effect on tumor control. The conclusion would be wrong if a prospective series at the recommended doses, with volume and selection controlled, failed to beat low-dose control at 2 to 3 years, or bought that control at a carotid cost that offsets it.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Durability, not early response, is where dose matters: 1y LC was flat across doses (P=.096) while 2y and 3y LC tracked dose (P<.01), with 45 Gy/5fx modeled at 41% 3y LC. Escalation is volume-gated (45 Gy/5fx ceiling for <25 cm3) and weighed against carotid blowout in up to 10% to 20%.

open_questions: Does concurrent systemic therapy shift the SBRT reRT dose-response?
Prospective validation of 40-50 Gy/5fx for recurrent H&N

sites.intro: Stage I NSCLC SBRT: modeled LC plateau doses by T stage and prescription point (PTV periphery vs isocenter).

studies.name: HyTEC Stage I NSCLC SBRT Local Control
studies.tldr: Modeled LC plateau at PTV periphery: 43±1 Gy/3 fx, 47±1 Gy/4 fx, 50±1 Gy/5 fx across 46 pooled SBRT series in stage I NSCLC.
details: 🔍 160 published SBRT series for stage I NSCLC screened (PubMed through May 2014)
🔍 46 studies met quality criteria; series with <10 pts, >T2, or oligometastatic disease excluded

details.text: 🔍 Pooled cohort by dose per fraction
subdetails: 3-4 Gy/fx: 211 pts from 3 studies, included to anchor the curve shoulder

details: 📊 1, 2, 3 and 5 yr LC fitted against BED with LQ, USC and regrowth models
📐 None of the models fit well by χ2/ndf; the regrowth model fit best
📐 Regrowth-fitted α/β ~25 Gy (T1), 19 Gy (T2), 21 Gy (T1+T2)

details.text: 📊 Regrowth model: dose needed to reach max TCP, by T stage and prescription point

details: 📊 LQ and USC models give near-identical T1+T2 PTV doses: 44±1, 47±1, 50±1 Gy for 3/4/5 fx
🔗 vs historic conventional RT (2-3 Gy/fx to ≈54-60 Gy): long-term LC ≈30-70%, OS ≈15-30%

details.text: ⚠️ Measurement caveats on the pooled LC
subdetails: Competing non-cancer deaths censored, so actuarial 1-3 yr LC may overestimate true LC
LC mostly radiographic; post-SBRT fibrosis and early FDG uptake confound recurrence calls
Most series report LC only to 3 yr; OS collected but not modeled
Surgical series count intralobar and nodal failures as local, so LC isn't comparable to resection

verdict.rationale: Study-level pooled modeling, not patient-level data; none of three TCP models fit well, and plateau doses are model outputs never tested prospectively.
verdict.audience: Medically inoperable stage I NSCLC, T1-T2, node-negative

studies.significance: Prescription convention gates transfer: the modeled LC plateau is 43, 47 and 50 Gy (±1) to the PTV periphery in 3, 4 and 5 fx but 54, 59 and 63 Gy at isocenter. T2 needs 45, 50 and 53 Gy at the PTV vs 42, 46 and 48 Gy for T1, so one size-blind schedule sits closer to the margin for T2.
studies.monday_clinic: In a medically inoperable, node-negative peripheral T1-T2 NSCLC planned for 3-5 fx SBRT, this places the LC plateau at PTV-periphery doses of 43-50 Gy, higher for T2; it does not extend to central or >5 cm tumors, which the pooled series underrepresent.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Systematic review of **160** published SBRT series (PubMed through May 2014) with **46** meeting quality criteria (N, dose homogeneity, follow-up, LC reporting). Study-level LC fitted to LQ, USC and regrowth TCP models as a function of BED.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Stage I NSCLC, T1-T2, largely **medically inoperable**. Series with <10 pts, tumors above T2, or oligometastatic lung disease excluded. **3268 pts** at ≥6 Gy/fx plus **211 pts** at 3-4 Gy/fx from 3 studies.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: SBRT/SABR in 3-5 fx; doses modeled both at isocenter and at the PTV covered by the **80% isodose line**. Typical ITV-to-PTV expansions 3-8 mm axial and 5-10 mm cranio-caudal.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Actuarial **local control** at 1, 2, 3 and 5 yr, defined as no local progression on CT or PET-CT. OS collected but not modeled; distant failure not recorded.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **Regrowth model fit best**, though none fit well. Fitted α/β ~25 Gy (T1), 19 Gy (T2), 21 Gy (T1+T2); dose to max TCP by stage and prescription point in the table above.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Historic conventional RT at 2-3 Gy/fx to ≈54-60 Gy gave long-term LC ≈30-70% and OS ≈15-30%, so the **steep dose-response** to ablative dosing is the anchor. ASTRO guidance conditionally extends SBRT to inoperable tumors >5 cm, a group this pooled data underrepresents.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents medically inoperable, node-negative T1-T2 NSCLC treated with 3-5 fx SBRT, mostly peripheral lesions ≤5 cm. Does not represent central or >5 cm tumors, or operable pts.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Censoring competing deaths in a frail cohort and radiographic LC calls after SBRT fibrosis both bias LC upward. Most series stop at 3 yr, and the literature ends May 2014.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The value is a **dose ceiling**: the curve locates where added dose stops buying LC, reframing escalation beyond it as toxicity cost. The **reporting standards** (dose algorithm, heterogeneity correction, GTV D95%, elapsed days) target the data heterogeneity behind the poor model fits.

studies.interpretation:
The useful output here is not the claim that stage I NSCLC responds to SBRT, which nobody disputes, but a dose-response curve that locates a plateau. Pooling 46 series and fitting LC against BED, the regrowth model places maximal LC at 43, 47 and 50 Gy (each ±1) to the PTV periphery for 3, 4 and 5 fractions. Against the historic conventionally fractionated benchmark the authors cite, with long-term LC of ≈30-70%, the steepness of the curve and the gain from ablative dosing are not in question. What the curve adds is a ceiling: it implies that above those doses a typical peripheral T1-T2 lesion gains little further control, which reframes escalation as a toxicity cost rather than a control gain.

Three features should temper how literally a planner takes the numbers. First, by the authors' own goodness-of-fit metric none of the three models fit well; regrowth was the best of a weak set, and its fitted α/β (~25 Gy for T1, ~19 Gy for T2) sits far above the value conventionally assumed for tumor. That matters because BED-based equivalence between schedules depends on exactly that parameter. Second, the inputs are study-level actuarial LC, not patient-level data, so within-series dose spread, tumor location and histology are averaged away. Third, the endpoint leans optimistic: competing non-cancer deaths are censored in a frail inoperable cohort, and radiographic assessment after SBRT is confounded by fibrosis and early FDG uptake. Both biases push reported LC upward and could make the plateau appear to arrive at a lower dose than it truly does.

The most practical point is the gap between isocenter and periphery. The same regrowth T1+T2 fit corresponds to 54, 59 and 63 Gy at isocenter with the 80% isodose covering the PTV, so a schedule quoted without its normalization convention cannot be placed on this curve, and two centers with the same nominal prescription may sit at different points on it. The T1/T2 split also matters: T2 needs 45, 50 and 53 Gy at the PTV versus 42, 46 and 48 Gy for T1, consistent with the lower fitted α/β for T2. A department running one schedule for every peripheral stage I lesion is, on this model, closer to the margin for its T2 tumors than for its T1 tumors.

What it does not settle is substantial. Central tumors and lesions above 5 cm were underrepresented and carry less favorable SBRT outcomes, so the plateau doses should not be carried over to them. OS was collected but inconsistently reported and not modeled, so nothing here speaks to survival tradeoffs at the plateau. Comparison with resection remains unequal, since surgical series count intralobar and nodal recurrences as local failure. The reporting standards table may prove the more durable contribution: the weak model fits are plausibly in part a data problem, and a future pooled analysis improves only if series report prescription physics, heterogeneity correction and target coverage consistently.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Prescription convention gates transfer: the modeled LC plateau is 43, 47 and 50 Gy (±1) to the PTV periphery in 3, 4 and 5 fx but 54, 59 and 63 Gy at isocenter. T2 needs 45, 50 and 53 Gy at the PTV vs 42, 46 and 48 Gy for T1, so one size-blind schedule sits closer to the margin for T2.

open_questions: Does dose above the modeled plateau add LC for T2 tumors?
Dose-response for central and >5 cm tumors
Validation of plateau doses in patient-level prospective data

sites.intro: Liver SBRT: G≥3 GI risk <10% at mean Rx 50 Gy in 3 to 6 fx; QUANTEC MLD limits judged still reasonable.

studies.name: HyTEC Liver SBRT Dose-Volume Effects
studies.tldr: Grade ≥3 GI D50 87.1 Gy and D10 50.6 Gy (Rx dose); liver-enzyme fit not significant (P = .10); QUANTEC MLD limits judged still reasonable.
details: 🔍 Pooled study-level review of published liver SBRT series; PubMed search through May 2014
🔍 Probit NTCP fits by maximum likelihood; physical dose used, no BED conversion
🔍 HCC, IHC and liver mets pooled; mostly 3 to 6 fx, one single-fraction series
📐 Liver-enzyme model: no dose response established (P = .10), 5 studies
📊 Mean Rx 50 Gy in 3 to 6 fx → G≥3 general GI risk <10%
📊 Series using the ≥700 cm3 sparing guideline (15 or 17 Gy): G≥3 GI 9.3% (11 of 118), 68% CI 6.6% to 12.8%

details.text: 🔗 vs QUANTEC MLD limits: G3 liver-enzyme risk <20% probability
subdetails: Primary liver: 13 Gy (3 fx), 18 Gy (6 fx)
Liver mets: 15 Gy (3 fx), 20 Gy (6 fx)

details: ⚠️ Rx dose stands in for duodenal, gastric and bowel dose; OAR DVHs not available
⚠️ General GI is a composite including fatigue and nausea, not organ-specific injury

subdetails: Bujold: 3 of 102 HCC pts died of liver failure without progression
Andolino: liver failure in 4 of 8 HCC pts with baseline CP ≥8

verdict.rationale: Study-level pooled data; prescription dose stands in for GI organ dose, physical dose without BED, and the liver-enzyme dose-response fit failed (P = .10).
verdict.audience: Liver SBRT for HCC, IHC or liver mets, mostly 3 to 6 fx

studies.significance: The usable planning number is GI, not liver: mean Rx 50 Gy in 3 to 6 fx kept modeled G≥3 GI risk <10%, and series using the ≥700 cm3 sparing guideline carried 9.3% G≥3 GI. Because the GI model runs on Rx dose, not duodenal or gastric DVH, it does not replace organ-level constraints for a central or hilar target.
studies.monday_clinic: In HCC or liver-met pts planned for 3 to 6 fx liver SBRT, this supports keeping QUANTEC MLD limits as the liver-enzyme guardrail; it does not address Child-Pugh decline or liver failure, which it did not model.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Quantitative review pooling published liver SBRT series that reported **both toxicity and dose-volume data** (PubMed through May 2014). **Probit NTCP** fits by maximum likelihood, profile-likelihood parameter CIs, bootstrap curve CIs (2000 samples). Overlapping cohorts reduced to the most recent report.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: HCC, IHC and liver metastases, **pooled**; metastatic and primary cohorts could not be modeled separately for lack of data. Fractionation concentrated at **3 to 6 fx**, plus one single-fraction series (Goodman).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Prescription typically covered the PTV with the **70% to 85% isodose line**, with 4DCT, abdominal compression or active breathing control for motion and fiducial tracking in some series. GTV excluded from the MLD calculation in all series except Son.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **G≥3 liver enzymes** (≥5x ULN ALT/AST, CTCAE v4.0) vs MLD; **G≥2 and G≥3 general GI** (fatigue, nausea, diarrhea, gastritis, ulcers, GI pain, colitis) vs Rx dose. Child-Pugh decline, RILD and liver failure too inconsistently reported to model.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Only the GI fits reached statistical significance; the liver-enzyme model could not exclude dose-independent risk (**P = .10**), possibly skewed by the Lee et al outlier.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Reaffirms the **QUANTEC** liver MLD limits (13 Gy/3 fx and 18 Gy/6 fx primary; 15 Gy/3 fx and 20 Gy/6 fx mets) as carrying G3 enzyme risk **<20%**. Velec et al suggested MLD **<18 Gy (6 fx)** when liver-function decline in HCC is the endpoint.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents liver SBRT in 3 to 6 fx for HCC, IHC or liver mets planned on physical dose. Does not represent reirradiation, organ-level GI constraints, or liver-function decline in cirrhotic pts.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Liver-enzyme model rests on **5 studies and 17/288 events**. The general GI composite counts fatigue alongside ulceration, softening the G≥2 curve. The 700 cm3 pooled rate carries only a 68% CI.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The paper reaffirms existing limits more than it derives new ones; its durable output is a **reporting standard** (liver minus GTV volumes, absolute DVHs, baseline CP and ALBI, explicit liver-failure reporting) that would let organ-level models replace Rx-dose surrogates.

studies.interpretation:
This is less a test of a hypothesis than an audit of whether the liver SBRT literature through 2014 could support dose-response modeling at all, and the answer splits by endpoint. For liver enzymes, the one endpoint where liver-specific dosimetry (MLD of liver minus GTV) was available, the probit fit failed: the model could not reject dose independence (P = .10), and the upper confidence bound on D50 runs to infinity. The tempting read is that MLD does not matter for SBRT. The better read is that 17 events across 288 pts in 5 series cannot resolve a dose response, particularly with metastatic and cirrhotic livers pooled and one series computing MLD with the GTV included.

The GI models did reach statistical significance, but they are built on the prescription dose rather than the dose to duodenum, stomach or bowel. That substitution is the central weakness. Two lesions prescribed the same dose can sit abutting the duodenum or well away from it, and the prescription carries none of that geometry. The G≥2 D10 of 18.4 Gy, a prescription well below the ablative range, mostly signals that the endpoint is soft: fatigue and nausea are counted alongside ulceration and colitis. The G≥3 model is more useful, and its anchor, mean Rx 50 Gy in 3 to 6 fx carrying under 10% risk, is a defensible population-level statement. It describes average geometry, though, and a central lesion near the hilum, which the authors flag as higher GI risk, is exactly where an average misleads.

Against QUANTEC, the paper reaffirms rather than revises. The QUANTEC MLD limits sit where the fitted enzyme curve stays below 20% probability, but because that curve is not statistically established, the reaffirmation rests partly on the absence of contrary evidence. The 700 cm3 sparing rule fares similarly: widely used as a planning heuristic, not analyzable here, represented only by a pooled 9.3% G≥3 GI rate (11 of 118) from series that used it. Velec et al's MLD limit of <18 Gy in 6 fx for liver-function decline in HCC points to the endpoint that matters most in cirrhotic pts and that this analysis could not model.

Liver failure, the endpoint that kills, sits outside the models entirely: 3 deaths among 102 HCC pts in one series, and failure in 4 of 8 pts starting at CP ≥8 in another. Those numbers argue that baseline liver function, not MLD, dominates risk in the worst-functioning livers, and a pooled study-level framework cannot see it. Modeling physical dose without BED conversion across single-fraction through 6 fx regimens also flattens real biological differences.

What would make the GI conclusions wrong is a modern series with organ-level DVHs showing that duodenal or gastric hot spots, not prescription, drive ulceration; Rx-based limits would then be a coincidence of typical lesion geometry rather than a constraint. The reporting standards the authors lay out (liver minus GTV volumes, absolute DVHs, baseline Child-Pugh and ALBI, explicit grading and cause of liver failure) are arguably the paper's most lasting contribution, because they define the data that would let the next analysis replace surrogates with organ dose.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: For constraint-setting, the GI fits are the actionable output: mean Rx 50 Gy in 3 to 6 fx modeled G≥3 GI risk <10%. The liver-enzyme model never established a dose response (P = .10), so QUANTEC MLD limits are reaffirmed rather than refined, and central tumors near the hilum still need organ-level GI planning.

open_questions: Organ-level duodenal and gastric constraints for liver SBRT
Toxicity differences between HCC, IHC and liver metastases
MLD limits for Child-Pugh decline in cirrhotic HCC
